basis: Localized aneurysmal retinal capillary lesion with exudation defines both ocular and vascular disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: retinal capillaries are vessels; their defining aneurysmal pathology qualifies without systemic vascular disease.

basis: Skeletal defects, cutis laxa and intellectual disability define syndrome; ptosis/strabismus occur in 30-79%. Enamel defects omitted at cap; hepatic adenoma is a separate neoplasm.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: enamel defects occur in 30-79% but are omitted at the four-axis cap, prioritizing ocular functional impairment.
decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis and strabismus are annotated in 30-79%, supporting common eyelid and ocular motor dysfunction.

basis: Gonadal dysgenesis causes endocrine failure; urethral malformations and skeletal bone loss are annotated in 80-99%. Gonadoblastoma is a separate neoplasm.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias and urogenital sinus anomalies are annotated in 80-99%; structural urethral malformation falls within renal.

basis: Plasma-cell neoplasm with defining osteosclerotic bone lesions; peripheral neuropathy accompanies roughly half of cases as a manifestation of the plasma-cell process.

decisions.neurologic: involved: peripheral neuropathy occurs in approximately 50% and reflects the plasma-cell disease, commonly expressed within POEMS.

basis: Benign perineurial nerve-sheath neoplasm characteristically arising in dermis or subcutis; both tissue origin and anatomical site qualify.

decisions.neurologic: primary: perineurial nerve-sheath origin qualifies under tumour-origin rules; extraneural growth does not require demonstrable nerve dysfunction.

basis: B-cell lymphoma arising in colonic mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue; colonic origin, blood-cell malignancy and lymphoma mechanism define the three axes.

decisions.haematologic: primary: this is a malignant B-lymphocyte disease, qualifying as blood-cell neoplasia despite its extranodal location.

basis: Inclusion-body myopathy and brain white-matter abnormalities define disease; ptosis impairs eyelid function in 4/11 patients (~36%).

decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis occurs in 4/11 (~36%); eyelids are explicitly ocular, and myopathic eyelid dysfunction qualifies.

basis: Acquired disorder of energy regulation causing obesity; antecedent hypothalamic injury is the cause rather than neurological damage produced by this metabolic condition.

decisions.neurologic: none: the underlying hypothalamic injury is an antecedent lesion; obesity does not itself establish additional brain damage.

basis: Defining hyaline deposition causes skin nodules (34/35), gingival overgrowth (33/35), contractures and osteolysis. Recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: gingival fibromatosis is a defining manifestation, present in 33/35 patients; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: RAG2-associated SCID causes failure of T- and B-lymphocyte development, defining both immunodeficiency and a blood-cell disorder; secondary infections do not add organs.

decisions.haematologic: primary: defective T- and B-cell development produces profound lymphocyte deficiency, meeting the explicit blood-cell disease rule.
